name: HumanEval_6_parse_nested_parens
completion:
# Split the input string into groups
  groups = paren_string.split(' ')
  
  # Initialize an array to store the maximum nesting level for each group
  max_levels = []
  
  # Iterate through each group
  groups.each do |group|
    # Initialize the current nesting level and maximum nesting level for the group
    current_level = 0
    max_level = 0
    
    # Iterate through each character in the group
    group.each_char do |char|
      # If the character is an opening parenthesis, increment the current nesting level
      if char == '('
        current_level += 1
      # If the character is a closing parenthesis, decrement the current nesting level
      elsif char == ')'
        current_level -= 1
      end
      
      # Update the maximum nesting level for the group
      max_level = [max_level, current_level].max
    end
    
    # Add the maximum nesting level for the group to the array
    max_levels << max_level
  end
  
  # Return the array of maximum nesting levels
  max_levels
end

name: HumanEval_10_make_palindrome
completion:
# Find the longest suffix of the string that is a palindrome
  # We iterate from the end of the string to the beginning
  # The first suffix we find that is a palindrome is the longest one
  suffix = string.dup
  suffix_len = string.length
  suffix_len.times do
    suffix = string[suffix_len - 1, 1]
    suffix_len -= 1
    # Check if the suffix is a palindrome
    if suffix == suffix.reverse
      break
    end
  end
  
  # The part of the string that is not part of the palindrome
  prefix = string[0, suffix_len]
  
  # Append the reverse of the prefix to the end of the string
  string + prefix.reverse
end

name: HumanEval_141_file_name_check
completion:
# Split the file name into parts
  parts = file_name.split('.')
  
  # Check if there is exactly one dot
  if parts.length != 2
    return 'No'
  end
  
  # Check if the substring before the dot starts with a letter and contains no more than 3 digits
  before_dot = parts[0]
  if before_dot.length == 0 || !before_dot.match?(/^\w/)
    return 'No'
  end
  
  # Count the number of digits in the file name
  digit_count = file_name.scan(/\d/).length
  if digit_count > 3
    return 'No'
  end
  
  # Check if the substring after the dot is one of the allowed extensions
  after_dot = parts[1]
  if !after_dot.match?(/^(txt|exe|dll)$/i)
    return 'No'
  end
  
  return 'Yes'
end

name: HumanEval_156_int_to_mini_roman
completion:
# Convert number to string
  number = number.to_s
  
  # Define Roman numeral mappings
  roman_numerals = {
    'M' => 1000,
    'CM' => 900,
    'D' => 500,
    'CD' => 400,
    'C' => 100,
    'XC' => 90,
    'L' => 50,
    'XL' => 40,
    'X' => 10,
    'IX' => 9,
    'V' => 5,
    'IV' => 4,
    'I' => 1
  }
  
  # Convert to lowercase
  roman_numerals = roman_numerals.map { |key, value| [key.downcase, value] }.to_h
  
  # Build the Roman numeral string
  result = ''
  number = number.to_i
  
  # Iterate through the Roman numeral mappings
  roman_numerals.each do |roman, value|
    while number >= value
      result += roman
      number -= value
    end
  end
  
  result
end
